title: Human Material Appearance and Vision Foundation Models
summary: Do frozen pretrained representations capture the way people judge glossiness, texture, and translucency in natural photographs? I compare human judgments with representations from 9 pretrained vision models.
methods: Psychophysical evaluation · Photograph-grouped nested cross-validation · Representation analysis · Material-category controls · Bootstrap inference
detail: The study includes 300 material regions, 35 observers, and 3,770 perceptual ratings, with stimulus-mean reliability of 0.91–0.97. Frozen features predict appearance ratings largely through material identity, with a small but reliable within-category signal; this motivates perceptually supervised adaptation.

title: Material Segmentation and Color Representations
summary: An investigation of how color-space representations and color-based augmentation influence material segmentation and learned feature representations.
methods: Semantic segmentation · Color spaces · Data augmentation · Feature representation analysis

title: Color-Based Augmentation for Skin Segmentation
summary: Collaborative research examining color transformations and color-space representations in deep-learning-based semantic skin segmentation.
methods: Deep learning · Semantic segmentation · Color transformations

title: Color Appearance of Fluorescent Materials
summary: An evaluation of the CIECAM02 color appearance model for fluorescent samples, building on my master's research on the effect of near-gray backgrounds.
methods: Color appearance modeling · Fluorescent samples · Background effects
